subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a per-spawn `sessions_spawn.env` API for ACP sessions, or keep env injection limited to configured/operator-trusted surfaces such as per-agent env or exec-only SecretRef?
rationale: The requested API can pass credential-like values from a model-callable tool into host ACP subprocesses, so maintainers must choose the trust model, validation, redaction, and session reuse semantics before implementation.

options.title: Design a safe ACP per-spawn env contract
options.body: Add the capability only with dangerous-key blocking, source limits, redaction, freshness/reuse rules, docs, and focused ACP/ACPX subprocess proof.

options.title: Route users to configured env surfaces
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` unchanged and make per-agent env or exec-only SecretRef the supported credential injection path once that work lands.

options.title: Reject per-spawn env injection
options.body: Close the issue as too broad if model-callable env injection is outside the intended OpenClaw security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design a safe ACP per-spawn env contract
recommendation.body: Add the capability only with dangerous-key blocking, source limits, redaction, freshness/reuse rules, docs, and focused ACP/ACPX subprocess proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the adjacent per-agent env contract and described the cross-surface requirements this decision needs.
